column1: Table S3c. Enclosure-stage SC priority operating regions
Priority operating regions (weight = 2) and IFC implementation evidence; all distances are scenario-modeling parameters.

column2: Spray and trowel mortar on designated unfinished interior wall surfaces.
column3: Mobile wall mortar spraying and plastering robot
column4: At all applicable unfinished interior wall faces on floors 1–3, continuous accessible working strips 0.5–2.0 m outward into the operating side; exclude wall solids, door/window openings and obstacles.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcWall/IfcWallStandardCase + IfcDoor and IfcWindow openings + IfcSlab; identify room-facing free side by geometric accessibility, since no IfcSpace is present. Evidence: IFC + unfinished-surface assumption

column2: Capture visual observations of applicable installed doors, windows and selected architectural elements.
column4: For all designated installed door and window targets on 1F–3F, accessible indoor-facing viewpoints 1.0–2.0 m from the relevant frame/panel, with only local adjustments and approach positions.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcDoor, IfcWindow, related IfcOpeningElement and walls; derive view direction/occlusion and reachable stations. Evidence: Direct + rule-derived

column2: Deliver finishing supplies from receiving/vertical-transfer points to occupied workrooms.
column4: 1F: west main entrance → central west–east corridor → north/south doors of assigned delivery rooms; 2F–3F: from accessible stair/lift transfer landing → central corridor and destination doors. Corridor buffer 0.75–1.0 m per side; 1.5 m radius at unloading/docking nodes.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcDoor, IfcWall/IfcWallStandardCase, IfcSlab, IfcStair/IfcStairFlight; rebuild traversability graph (no IfcSpace). Delivery targets and vertical freight means assumed. Evidence: IFC + transport targets

column2: Detect, plan and perform adaptive filling/caulking along applicable architectural joints.
column4: Across floors 1–3, include ALL applicable door-frame/wall perimeter joints, window-frame/wall perimeter joints, identifiable prefabricated wall-panel seams and specified expansion/sealant joints; accessible-side continuous strips 0.5–1.5 m from each joint; union of all eligible strips.
column5: IFC: IfcDoor, IfcWindow, IfcWall/IfcWallStandardCase, IfcOpeningElement and IfcRelFillsElement; derive candidate boundaries geometrically. Only demonstrated panel seams or explicitly assumed sealant joints included; ordinary wall intersections alone are not proof of a sealant joint. Evidence: IFC-derived candidates + sealant assumption

column2: Lay and align floor tiles over major contiguous public circulation and other designated first-floor finishing areas.
column4: 1F main indoor public flooring area: west entrance vestibule, connected lobby/foyer, longitudinal central corridor and connected public circulation floor surfaces; may include additional suitable general-purpose 1F floors if the assumed finish is tiled. Prioritize the full assigned tiling workface, excluding walls, stair voids, service shafts and non-tiled rooms.
column5: IFC: 1F IfcSlab + IfcWall + IfcDoor; reconstruct indoor accessible floor polygons and public connectivity. No IfcSpace/IfcCovering, so room labels and tile finish must be explicitly assigned. Evidence: IFC-constrained finishing assumption

column2: Clean stair treads and intermediate landings during construction finishing or pre-handover.
column4: Both west and east stair cores: all applicable stair treads and intermediate landings on the usable floor connections; include accessible entry/exit/turning footprints within approximately 1.0 m of stair transitions.
column5: Direct IFC: IfcStair and IfcStairFlight plus adjacent IfcSlab landing solids; use true 3D elevations. Evidence: Direct + rule-derived

column2: Inventory and localize finishing materials at distributed indoor temporary storage rooms.
column4: Six distinct temporary storage rooms: one feasible room near each west/east building end on each of 1F, 2F and 3F. Retain 0.5–1.5 m accessible patrol aisles beside material stacks, rack-facing stations and door-to-aisle links; not the whole rooms by default.
column5: IFC-constrained room selection: reconstruct rooms from IfcWall, IfcDoor and IfcSlab (no IfcSpace). Choose six distinct rooms satisfying size, load, access and egress requirements. Evidence: Assumed six rooms; IFC-constrained

column2: Identify and presort light finishing/packaging waste at distributed indoor collection rooms.
column4: Six distinct presorting rooms: one near each west/east building end on each of 1F–3F, mutually exclusive with E-SC7 rooms. Prioritize 1.5–2.0 m radius around each waste receiving/sorting station and doorway-to-station access; use ground floor for subsequent centralized removal.
column5: IFC-constrained room selection: IfcWall, IfcDoor, IfcSlab; reconstruct accessible rooms and station footprints; require ventilation/fire safety, load and egress clearances. Evidence: Assumed six rooms; IFC-constrained

column1: Label: Note Priority definition: Priority regions represent planning-level robot working positions and repeatedly traversed corridors, not verified trajectories; buffers/station radii are study-defined, not universal values. Design status: Floor-specific assumption Temporary-facility assumption: 1F–3F east/west six material and six waste zones are per stage, not 12 different scenarios. IFC scope: No IfcSpace or IfcCovering in the inspected enclosure file; building-use labels and finishes are assumptions. Literature evidence: References support task and general workspace principles; exact geometry and 2:1 weights require experimental validation.
